videos.title: Antelopower LA35 ride and range test, singletrack and enduro with minimal commentary.
videos.description:
This is a typical ride for me. Typical pace and terrain. I was riding fairly conservatively and not trying to kill the battery.  Temps were around 60 degrees F but the battery did start out at 38 degrees F. I rode gently until the battery came up to temp. I did the same ride 2 days in a row with two different batteries.  Day 1 was 11.7 miles, 2:30 moving time, battery from 100 to 25 percent (rode in a big group, more rock terrain).  Day 2  was 13.5 miles, 2 hr moving time, battery from 100 to 21 percent (slightly faster pace, less rock more singletrack).   

From what ive gathered the battery should last about 10 miles or 1.5 hours at full race pace.

videos.title: Thoughts without a Thinker with Mark Epstein
videos.description:
Thirty-one years ago, when the book "Thoughts without a Thinker: Psychotherapy from a Buddhist Perspective" came out, Buddhism and psychotherapy were not the obvious pairing they are today. Author Mark Epstein was an early voice in explaining how Buddhism is relevant to psychotherapy. Drawing on his own clinical work and personal experience, he showed how Buddhist meditation and methods of analytic inquiry into the self are fundamentally aligned with the practice of psychotherapy. Going further, he pointed out that while psychotherapy can identify what ails us, it doesn’t offer a path to freedom from the self’s craving. Buddhism does. 

Yes, Buddhism teaches there is no self, but Epstein argues that we have to uncover how the self appears in order to diminish its hold. Yes, the goal of Buddhism is to find freedom from the suffering of samsara—the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth—but Buddhist wisdom can have a concrete impact on everyday life.

The landmark Thoughts without a Thinker was recently re-released with a new preface by Epstein. On November 9, 20,26 Epstein joined us for an interview about this influential book and its enduring relevance.

Życie w permanentnej poczekalni (metafora stacji kolejowej z ciągle przesuwanym rozkładem jazdy i zakurzonymi walizkami).
Rezygnacja z edukacji, kariery, stabilności finansowej i emerytur w oczekiwaniu na rychły koniec świata.

videos.title: The Fed Is About To Make Bitcoin Explode | Nik Bhatia
videos.description:
Nik Bhatia believes Bitcoin's bear market already bottomed over the summer. But the bigger question is why Bitcoin hasn't exploded higher yet. Nik, macro analyst and author of Layered Money and Bitcoin Age, joins Pete Rizzo to explain why liquidity has been negative throughout 2026, why the old model of Federal Reserve QE may be over, and what macro trigger could finally pull Bitcoin out of its grind.

His case starts with the price. Nik sees the low-$70,000 range as the key level keeping the bottoming thesis intact and argues that Bitcoin's recent price action looks increasingly constructive. Bad news is having less impact, institutional adoption continues through firms like BlackRock, Fidelity, Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan, and he believes the worst of the bear market is likely behind us. But he still isn't calling for an immediate explosion higher. In his view, Bitcoin may need to grind until macro liquidity turns.

That leads directly to the Fed. Nik argues the Bernanke-Powell version of QE — simply printing money to buy longer-duration Treasuries — may be finished. Instead, he points to the Fed's move toward T-bill purchases and what he calls "T-bill QE," arguing that balance sheet expansion is ultimately necessary to keep the system functioning. He even lays out a longer-term possibility where Fed balance sheet growth becomes tied to nominal GDP rather than arriving only in massive crisis-driven waves.

The problem today is liquidity. Nik says his liquidity index has been negative throughout 2026, with a global dollar squeeze keeping financial conditions tight. Foreign dollar-denominated debt creates persistent demand for dollars, and in his framework liquidity can't sustainably turn positive until the dollar stops rising.
